PANCE Imaging Findings - Summary Chart 
Reading approach + high-yield disease findings: CXR, KUB, CT, US (incl. FAST), Echo, MRI, and others 
PANCE relevance:   'Using Diagnostic and Laboratory Studies' = 10% of the 2025 NCCPA blueprint, with skills in   selecting appropriate diagnostic studies   and   reviewing/interpreting results . Findings below are recurring
buzzwords across PA prep resources. 
Chest X-Ray (CXR) 
Reading Approach (RIPE technical adequacy   →   ABCDE-FGHI) 
RIPE   =   R otation (clavicles equidistant from spinous process),   I nspiration ( ≥ 9-10 posterior or 5-6 anterior ribs above diaphragm),   P enetration (vertebral bodies just visible behind heart),   E xposure (PA vs AP - AP magnifies
heart; erect vs supine). 
A - Airway:   trachea midline; carina; ETT tip ~4 cm above carina. 
B - Bones / soft tissue:   rib fractures, lytic lesions, rib notching, subQ air, breast shadows. 
C - Cardiac:   CT ratio <50% on PA (<60% on AP); contour; valves; pacemaker leads. 
D - Diaphragm:   R higher than L by ~1-2 cm; sharp costophrenic angles;   free air under diaphragm = perforation . 
E - Effusions / Everything else:   pleural lines, thickening, fluid. 
F - Fields (lung):   symmetry, opacities, vascular markings, masses, nodules. 
G - Gastric bubble   under L hemidiaphragm. 
H - Hila:   L higher than R; lymphadenopathy; calcifications. 
I - Lines / tubes / devices. 
Finding   Disease   Clinical Implication / Next Step
INFECTIONS / INFILTRATES 
Lobar consolidation + air bronchograms   Bacterial pneumonia (typical, S. pneumoniae)   CURB-65 risk; outpatient macrolide/doxy or inpatient   β -lactam + macrolide 
Bulging fissure   (RUL)   Klebsiella pneumonia (alcoholic, currant-jelly sputum)   Inpatient, broad-spectrum antibiotics 
Bilateral diffuse interstitial / ground-glass   Atypical pneumonia (Mycoplasma); PCP in HIV   Macrolide for Mycoplasma; TMP-SMX + steroids for PCP 
Apical fibronodular opacities, upper-lobe cavitation   Reactivation tuberculosis   Airborne isolation;   RIPE   therapy 
Calcified parenchymal nodule   (Ghon focus) ± ipsilateral hilar node (Ranke
complex)
Healed primary TB   Latent infection; treat per IGRA/PPD 
Diffuse 1-3 mm 'millet seed' nodules   Miliary TB (hematogenous)   Same as active TB; consider HIV testing 
CHRONIC / DIFFUSE LUNG DISEASE 
Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy   ± reticular markings   Sarcoidosis (Stage I/II)   ACE level, biopsy non-caseating granulomas; steroids if symptomatic 
Honeycombing, basal/peripheral reticulation   (HRCT)   Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (UIP)   Antifibrotics: pirfenidone, nintedanib 
Hyperinflation, flat diaphragms,   ↑   AP diameter   COPD / emphysema   Bronchodilators, smoking cessation 
Eggshell hilar node calcification   Silicosis (industrial dust)   Smoking cessation;   ↑   TB risk 
Lower-lobe reticulonodular + pleural plaques   Asbestosis   Risk of mesothelioma, lung CA 
Pleural-based mass with effusion ± plaques   Mesothelioma   Thoracoscopic biopsy 
AIR / FLUID IN PLEURAL SPACE 
Visible pleural line, absent lung markings beyond   Pneumothorax   Needle decompression if tension; chest tube 
Tracheal deviation AWAY from white-out   Tension pneumothorax   Immediate needle decompression (2nd ICS MCL or 4th-5th ICS AAL) 
Tracheal deviation TOWARD white-out   Atelectasis / pneumonectomy / mucous plug   Bronchoscopy / re-expansion 
Blunting of costophrenic angle, meniscus sign   Pleural effusion (>200 mL on PA)   Thoracentesis if symptomatic; Light's criteria for exudate 
CARDIAC / VASCULAR / PE

Finding   Disease   Clinical Implication / Next Step 
Kerley B lines, cephalization, peribronchial cuffing, bat-wing/butterfly
opacity, cardiomegaly 
CHF / pulmonary edema   Diuresis; echo to characterize HFrEF vs HFpEF 
Widened mediastinum (>8 cm AP at aortic knob)   Aortic dissection / mediastinal hematoma   Emergent CTA chest 
Globular / water-bottle heart with clear lungs   Large pericardial effusion   Echo; pericardiocentesis if tamponade 
Westermark sign   (focal oligemia) /   Hampton hump   (wedge pleural-based
opacity)
Pulmonary embolism (CXR insensitive)   Get CTPA or V/Q scan 
Diffuse bilateral alveolar infiltrates with normal heart size   ARDS (PCWP <18, P/F <300)   Lung-protective ventilation (6 mL/kg IBW) 
EMERGENCIES / OTHER 
Free air under right hemidiaphragm   Pneumoperitoneum (perforation)   Surgical consult 
Spiculated solid pulmonary nodule >8 mm, upper lobe   Lung cancer (adenocarcinoma if peripheral)   CT, PET, biopsy; Fleischner criteria 
Cavitary lesion with central necrosis   Squamous cell lung CA, abscess, TB   Tissue diagnosis 
PEDIATRIC / CONGENITAL CXR SIGNS 
Steeple sign   (subglottic narrowing on AP)   Croup   (parainfluenza)   Humidified air, dexamethasone, racemic epi if stridor at rest 
Thumbprint sign   on lateral neck   Acute epiglottitis   (Hib historically; now mostly other
org) 
Airway control before any procedures ; do NOT examine without anesthesia/ENT 
Boot-shaped heart   (coeur en sabot)   Tetralogy of Fallot   Surgical repair 
Egg on a string   with narrow mediastinum   Transposition of the great arteries   Prostaglandin E1; surgery (arterial switch) 
Snowman / figure of 8   Supracardiac TAPVR   Emergent surgical repair 
Figure of 3 sign / rib notching   Coarctation of the aorta   Surgical or balloon repair

Abdominal X-Ray (KUB) 
Reading Approach 
Confirm view   - upright present? (Free air best on upright CXR or L lateral decubitus) 
Bowel gas pattern:   small bowel = central,   valvulae conniventes cross full lumen , dilated >3 cm. Large bowel = peripheral 'picture frame',   haustra do NOT cross full diameter , dilated >6 cm (>9 cm at cecum). 
Air-fluid levels   on upright (>2.5 cm or stepladder = obstruction). 
Free air:   under diaphragm;   Rigler sign   (gas on both sides of bowel wall);   football sign   in infants. 
Solid organs:   liver, spleen, kidney shadows, psoas margins. 
Calcifications:   aorta (AAA), phleboliths, renal/ureteral stones, gallstones (~10-15% radiopaque), pancreatic, appendicolith. 
Bones   (vertebral compression, lytic lesions) and   foreign bodies / lines . 
Finding   Disease   Clinical Implication / Next Step 
Centrally dilated loops with valvulae conniventes; stepladder air-fluid
levels; absent colonic gas 
Small bowel obstruction (SBO)   NPO, NGT, IVF; CT to localize transition; surgery if ischemia 
Peripheral colon >6 cm with haustra; cecum >9 cm   Large bowel obstruction   CT; surgical consult 
Diffuse small + large bowel dilation, no transition, post-op   Paralytic ileus   Supportive (correct K+/Mg, hold opiates) 
Coffee-bean / inverted-U sign pointing to RUQ   Sigmoid volvulus (older, debilitated)   Sigmoidoscopic decompression then sigmoidectomy 
Distended loop pointing to LUQ   Cecal volvulus   Surgery 
Transverse colon >6 cm with thumbprinting   Toxic megacolon (UC, C. difficile)   Bowel rest, IV steroids; emergent colectomy if perforation 
Free air under diaphragm; Rigler / double-wall sign; football sign in
infants 
Pneumoperitoneum (perforation)   Emergent surgical exploration 
Air in biliary tree + SBO + ectopic gallstone (Rigler triad)   Gallstone ileus   Stone removal; address fistula 
Radiopaque stone along ureter, hydroureter   Nephrolithiasis (Ca-oxalate ~80% opaque)   Non-contrast CT confirms;   ≤ 5 mm pass spontaneously 
Curvilinear calcified aortic shadow >3 cm   Abdominal aortic aneurysm   US screening; CTA if symptomatic; repair   ≥ 5.5 cm 
Calcified RLQ density (appendicolith)   Suggests appendicitis   CT with contrast 
Pancreatic calcifications   Chronic pancreatitis   Stool elastase; alcohol cessation; ERCP for ductal disease 
Non-Contrast Head CT 
Reading Approach 
Confirm   non-contrast   (so blood/calcium not confused with contrast). 
Symmetry   - gray-white differentiation, ventricles, sulci, basal cisterns. 
Blood   - look for hyperdensity 60-80 HU (epidural / subdural / SAH / IPH / IVH). 
Brain   - gray-white preservation, sulcal effacement, mass effect, midline shift. 
Cisterns   - basal/suprasellar (5-pointed star); effaced = herniation risk. 
Ventricles   - symmetric size; trapped temporal horn = early hydrocephalus. 
Bone window   - skull fracture, sinuses, mastoids. 
Soft tissue / scalp   - hematoma, foreign body. 
Finding   Disease   Clinical Implication / Next Step 
Lens-shaped (biconvex) hyperdensity, does NOT cross suture lines ;
usually temporal 
Epidural hematoma   (middle meningeal artery; lucid
interval)
Emergent neurosurgical evacuation 
Crescent-shaped hyperdensity, CROSSES sutures   but not midline   Subdural hematoma   (bridging veins; elderly,
alcoholic, anticoagulated)
Evacuation if symptomatic / >10 mm thick / >5 mm midline shift 
Hyperdensity in basal cisterns / Sylvian fissure / sulci   Subarachnoid hemorrhage   (aneurysmal; ACom
most common)
'Thunderclap headache'; CTA for aneurysm; nimodipine; coil/clip. If CT negative >6 h
post-onset   →   LP for xanthochromia

Finding   Disease   Clinical Implication / Next Step 
Round/oval hyperdensity within parenchyma   Intraparenchymal hemorrhage (HTN basal ganglia;
amyloid angiopathy lobar; AVM)
BP control; reverse anticoagulation; neurosurg consult 
Hyperdense MCA sign, loss of gray-white differentiation, insular ribbon
sign, sulcal effacement 
Acute ischemic stroke (early CT signs <6 h)   tPA if <4.5 h and no contraindications; thrombectomy if LVO <24 h 
Wedge-shaped hypodensity respecting vascular territory   Established/subacute ischemic stroke   Antiplatelet, statin, etiology workup 
Effaced 4th ventricle, posterior fossa hyperdensity   Cerebellar hemorrhage   Surgical evacuation if >3 cm or brainstem compression 
Ring-enhancing lesion(s)   (with contrast)   Brain abscess; toxoplasmosis (HIV); GBM; metastasis   MRI characterizes; biopsy or empiric therapy by context

Chest CT (CT-PA / CTA) 
Finding   Disease   Clinical Implication / Next Step 
Intraluminal filling defect in pulmonary artery   (CT-PA)   Pulmonary embolism   (gold standard)   Anticoagulation (LMWH/DOAC); thrombolysis if hemodynamically unstable 
RV strain, septal flattening, RV/LV ratio >1   Massive / submassive PE   Consider thrombolysis; ICU 
Intimal flap with two lumens in aorta   (CTA)   Aortic dissection (Stanford A = ascending; B =
descending)
Esmolol then nitroprusside; surgery for type A or complicated B 
Saccular/fusiform thoracic aortic dilation >5.5 cm   Thoracic aortic aneurysm   Surgical repair (Marfan, bicuspid AV at lower threshold) 
Tree-in-bud opacities, centrilobular nodules   Endobronchial spread (TB, MAC, aspiration)   Cultures; targeted therapy 
Subpleural reticulation + honeycombing, basal predominance   UIP / IPF   Antifibrotics (pirfenidone, nintedanib) 
Anterior mediastinal mass   '4 T's': Thymoma, Teratoma, Thyroid, Terrible
lymphoma
Tissue diagnosis 
Abdomen / Pelvis CT 
Finding   Disease   Clinical Implication / Next Step 
Dilated blind-ending appendix >6 mm, periappendiceal fat stranding, ±
appendicolith 
Acute appendicitis   Appendectomy; antibiotics if perforated/abscess (drain) 
Sigmoid wall thickening, pericolonic fat stranding, adjacent diverticula   Acute diverticulitis   Outpatient PO antibiotics (uncomplicated); IV abx ± drainage if abscess 
Transition point in dilated SB; whirl/whirlpool sign   Closed-loop SBO / volvulus   →   ischemia risk   Emergent surgery 
Bowel wall thickening, pneumatosis intestinalis, portal venous gas   Bowel ischemia   Emergent laparotomy 
Aortic diameter   ≥ 3 cm ; rupture   →   retroperitoneal hematoma   Abdominal aortic aneurysm   Repair if   ≥ 5.5 cm, growth >0.5 cm/6 mo, or symptomatic 
Hyperdense calculus in ureter; hydroureter, hydronephrosis,
perinephric stranding 
Ureterolithiasis   Tamsulosin; lithotripsy / ureteroscopy if >10 mm or obstructing 
Dilated CBD with stone in distal duct   Choledocholithiasis   ERCP 
Pancreatic enlargement, peripancreatic fluid, fat stranding ± necrosis   Acute pancreatitis (Balthazar grade)   Aggressive IVF; NPO; address cause (gallstones / alcohol) 
String sign (terminal ileum narrowing)   Crohn disease   Anti-TNF, biologics; mesalamine for mild 
Hepatic hypodensity with rim enhancement   Pyogenic abscess vs metastasis   Drain abscess; oncology workup if mets

Ultrasound (US) - General Principles 
Reading Approach & Echogenicity Cheat 
Probes:   curvilinear   (low-frequency, deep abdominal) - FAST/biliary/AAA/renal;   phased array   (small footprint, cardiac/subxiphoid);   linear   (high-frequency, superficial) - vascular, soft tissue, lung pleura, DVT. 
Anechoic   (black) = simple fluid (cyst, urine, bile, blood acutely). 
Hypoechoic   (dark gray) = complex fluid, abscess, solid hypoechoic mass. 
Hyperechoic   (bright) = fat, calcification, gas -   stones cast posterior acoustic shadow . 
Orientation:   probe indicator   →   patient's right (transverse) or head (longitudinal); cephalad = top of screen. 
DVT US   - cornerstone is   compressibility ; non-compressible vein = thrombus. 
FAST & eFAST Exam 
Indications, Probe, Sequence, Performance 
Indications:   blunt abdominal trauma (especially hypotensive); rapid bedside triage when CT not feasible. Helps decide OR vs CT in unstable patients. Less reliable for penetrating trauma. 
Probe:   curvilinear or phased-array   for the four standard FAST views;   linear   probe for the eFAST anterior chest views (pneumothorax). 
Sequence (typical):   1. Pericardial (subxiphoid)   →   2. RUQ (Morison's pouch)   →   3. LUQ (perisplenic)   →   4. Suprapubic. Add bilateral anterior chest views =   eFAST . 
Performance:   sensitivity ~80% / specificity >90% for hemoperitoneum; minimum detectable free fluid ~ 200-250 mL . Trendelenburg may improve sensitivity in RUQ. 
Key limitation:   a   negative FAST does NOT rule out injury . In stable patients with concerning mechanism / exam, get CT. Serial FAST may detect evolving hemorrhage. 
For pneumothorax:   US sensitivity ~88-90% (better than supine CXR ~50%); specificity ~99%.   For hemothorax:   US can detect as little as ~20 mL of pleural fluid. 
View   Probe Placement / Landmark   What to Look For   Pearls / Pitfalls 
1. Pericardial 
(subxiphoid; alt. parasternal)
Probe just inferior & right of xiphoid, indicator to
patient's   right , beam aimed toward   left shoulder ; use
liver as acoustic window. Alternative: parasternal long
axis. 
Anechoic stripe   in pericardial sac   →   pericardial effusion.   RV
diastolic collapse   +   RA systolic collapse   +   plethoric IVC   → 
tamponade physiology.
Distinguish pericardial from pleural fluid using descending aorta as
landmark (pericardial is anterior to descending aorta on PSLA).
Epicardial fat pad can mimic small effusion - usually anterior only. 
2. RUQ 
(Morison's pouch /
hepatorenal)
Mid-axillary line, ~10th-11th intercostal space,
indicator   cephalad . Visualize liver tip, hepatorenal
recess ( Morison's pouch ), and right
hemidiaphragm/subphrenic space. 
Most sensitive view   for hemoperitoneum in supine patient.
Anechoic stripe between liver & kidney = free fluid. Also
assess   above diaphragm   for hemothorax (anechoic above
bright diaphragm).
Sweep through entire interface; small fluid pockets often at hepatic
tip or caudal to liver. Perinephric fat may mimic free fluid (perirenal fat
is hypoechoic but follows kidney contour). 
3. LUQ 
(splenorenal / perisplenic)
More posterior & cephalad than RUQ - 'knuckles to
the bed', ~8th-10th intercostal space at posterior
axillary line, indicator   cephalad . Spleen as window.
Free fluid often appears   between spleen and diaphragm
(subphrenic)   first - look there before splenorenal interface.
Also assess above diaphragm for hemothorax.
Spleen is smaller and more posterior than liver - rib shadows
commonly obscure view; reposition probe between rib spaces.
Stomach gas is a confounder. 
4. Suprapubic 
(pelvic / pouch of Douglas)
Just superior to pubic symphysis in midline; rock
probe down into pelvis. Scan   both transverse &
longitudinal . Best with   full bladder   (acoustic
window). 
Free fluid in pouch of Douglas (rectouterine, F)   or 
rectovesical pouch (M) . In females also evaluate for IUP vs
ectopic in setting of pregnancy + trauma.
Empty bladder = poor view; consider clamping Foley if needed.
Pelvic free fluid is normal in small amounts in reproductive-age
females (physiologic). Bowel gas can mimic or obscure. 
5. eFAST - Anterior chest 
(pneumothorax) 
Linear   probe, midclavicular line at 2nd-4th intercostal
spaces bilaterally, indicator   cephalad . Identify pleural
line between two ribs ('bat sign'). 
Lung sliding   (pleural line shimmers with respiration) =   NO
pneumothorax . Absent sliding + 'barcode/stratosphere sign'
on M-mode =   pneumothorax .   Lung point   (transition between
sliding and non-sliding) is pathognomonic.
Bullae, pleural adhesions, mainstem intubation, prior pleurodesis   → 
false absent sliding. Sensitivity ~88-90%, specificity ~99%. Confirm
with upright CXR or CT if equivocal.

Non-Trauma Ultrasound Findings 
Finding   Disease   Clinical Implication / Next Step
ABDOMEN / PELVIS 
Gallstones with posterior acoustic shadowing, GB wall >3 mm,
pericholecystic fluid, sonographic Murphy 
Acute cholecystitis   NPO, IV antibiotics, cholecystectomy 
GB wall thickening alone (no stones), critically ill   Acalculous cholecystitis   Percutaneous cholecystostomy

pregnancy)
Appendectomy

VASCULAR / SOFT TISSUE / NECK

enhancement

IUP confirmed:   intrauterine gestational sac with yolk sac (~5-6 wk); FHT by

Intrauterine pregnancy   Routine OB care 
Empty uterus + adnexal mass + free fluid +   β -hCG above discriminatory
zone

Echocardiogram (TTE) 
Reading Approach 
Confirm views   - parasternal long-axis, short-axis (mitral / papillary / apex), apical 4/2/3/5-chamber, subxiphoid, suprasternal. 
Chamber sizes   - LV (LVEDD, LVESD), RV (>1:1 with LV = dilated), LA, RA. 
Wall thickness   - septum, posterior wall (>11 mm = LVH). 
Systolic function (LVEF):   HFrEF   ≤ 40% / HFmrEF 41-49% / HFpEF   ≥ 50%. 
Regional wall motion   - 17-segment model; akinesis/hypokinesis suggests prior MI in coronary distribution. 
Diastolic function   - E/A ratio, E/e' (>14 elevated), TR jet for PASP. 
Valves   - morphology, regurg jets (color Doppler), gradient/area (CW Doppler). 
Pericardium ,   aortic root ,   IVC   (size & collapse for volume status). 
Finding   Disease   Clinical Implication / Next Step 
Dilated LV with EF   ≤ 40%, global hypokinesis   HFrEF / dilated cardiomyopathy   GDMT: ARNI/ACEI,   β -blocker, MRA, SGLT2i; ICD if EF   ≤ 35% 
Preserved EF   ≥ 50%, elevated E/e', LA enlargement, LVH   HFpEF   Diuresis, treat HTN, SGLT2i 
Asymmetric septal hypertrophy, SAM of MV, dynamic LVOT obstruction   Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy   β -blocker; avoid dehydration / vasodilators; mavacamten / myectomy 
Calcified AV: peak velocity   ≥ 4 m/s, mean gradient   ≥ 40 mmHg, AVA   ≤ 1.0
cm² 
Severe aortic stenosis   AVR (TAVR if high surgical risk) 
MV thickening, hockey-stick deformity, MV area   ≤ 1.5 cm²   Mitral stenosis (most often rheumatic)   Anticoagulate if AF; balloon valvuloplasty 
Eccentric MR jet, dilated LA/LV   Mitral regurgitation   Surgery if symptomatic or EF declining 
Mobile echodensity (vegetation) on valve, regurgitation, abscess   Infective endocarditis   Modified Duke criteria; IV antibiotics ± surgery 
RWMA in coronary distribution, thinned scar, ± apical
aneurysm/thrombus 
Prior MI   Anticoagulate if thrombus; revascularization assessment 
Effusion + RV diastolic collapse, RA systolic collapse, plethoric IVC   Cardiac tamponade   Pericardiocentesis 
RV dilation, septal flattening, McConnell sign (apical sparing)   Acute PE with RV strain   CTPA; thrombolysis if massive 
LA mass attached to fossa ovalis, ball-on-stalk   Atrial myxoma   Surgical excision 
Apical ballooning post-emotional stress, EF recovers   Takotsubo (stress) cardiomyopathy   Supportive; rule out CAD

MRI - When MRI > CT 
Brain:   MS plaques, ischemic stroke beyond first hours (DWI), posterior fossa, tumor characterization, dementia workup.   Spine:   cord compression, cauda equina, disc herniation, spondylodiscitis.   MSK: 
meniscus / ACL tears, rotator cuff, labrum, AVN of femoral head (early), stress fracture, osteomyelitis.   Avoid with:   pacemakers (most), metallic ocular foreign body. 
Finding   Disease   Clinical Implication / Next Step 
Periventricular ovoid T2/FLAIR lesions perpendicular to ventricles
('Dawson fingers') ; lesions disseminated in time/space
Multiple sclerosis   DMT (ocrelizumab, etc.); MRI brain & spine 
Restricted diffusion on DWI, dark on ADC   Acute ischemic stroke (most sensitive in first hours)   Stroke pathway 
Cord T2 hyperintensity with vertebral body abnormality compressing
cord 
Metastatic spinal cord compression   Steroids, urgent radiation/surgery 
Disc herniation effacing nerve root or thecal sac with saddle anesthesia
/ retention 
Cauda equina syndrome   Emergent decompression 
Crescent-shaped subchondral T1 hypointensity in femoral head   Avascular necrosis (steroids, alcohol, sickle cell)   Core decompression vs arthroplasty 
Bone marrow edema (T2 hyperintense, T1 hypointense), ± sinus tract   Osteomyelitis   Cultures; IV antibiotics 4-6 weeks 
Other Modalities 
Modality   Key Findings & Interpretation   PANCE Pearls 
Mammography   (BI-RADS 0-6)   0 = incomplete; 1 = negative; 2 = benign; 3 = probably benign (6 mo f/u, <2% malignancy);   4 = suspicious
- biopsy   (4A low / 4B intermediate / 4C high);   5 = highly suggestive of malignancy (>95%) - biopsy ; 6
= known biopsy-proven cancer
Suspicious findings:   spiculated mass, pleomorphic clustered
microcalcifications, architectural distortion, skin/nipple retraction . Density
a-d (d = extremely dense   →   reduced sensitivity) 
HIDA scan   GB normally visualizes within 30-60 min.   Non-visualization at 1-4 h = acute cholecystitis . EF <35-40% 
→   chronic cholecystitis / biliary dyskinesia
Use when US is equivocal but suspicion remains 
V/Q scan   Ventilation/perfusion   mismatch   (perfusion defect with normal ventilation) = high probability PE   Use when CT-PA contraindicated (renal failure, contrast allergy, pregnancy) 
Bone scan   Multiple 'hot spots' = metastases (prostate, breast, lung). Diffuse skull/pelvis uptake =   Paget disease . 'Hot
nose' on cerebral perfusion scan = brain death sign
Bone pain + known cancer   →   bone scan first; MRI for cord compression risk 
Barium swallow   Bird's beak   at LES with proximal dilation   →   achalasia
Apple-core   annular narrowing   →   esophageal/colonic carcinoma 
Corkscrew   esophagus   →   diffuse esophageal spasm 
Schatzki ring   →   intermittent dysphagia for solids
Use water-soluble contrast (Gastrografin) if perforation suspected; barium
causes peritonitis 
Upper GI / barium enema   String sign of Kantor   (terminal ileum)   →   Crohn disease
Lead-pipe colon   (haustral loss)   →   chronic   UC
Apple-core lesion   →   colorectal carcinoma
Largely replaced by colonoscopy and CT enterography in practice 
DEXA   (T-score, WHO criteria)   Normal:   T   ≥   -1.0 
Osteopenia:   -1.0 to -2.5 
Osteoporosis:   ≤   -2.5 
Severe (established):   ≤   -2.5 + fragility fracture
USPSTF: screen women   ≥ 65 (or younger if elevated FRAX). T-score for
postmenopausal women / men   ≥ 50; Z-score otherwise (Z   ≤   -2.0 = below
expected for age)

Bamboo spine   Spine X-ray   Ankylosing spondylitis 
Pencil-in-cup deformity   (DIPs)   Hand X-ray   Psoriatic arthritis 
Chondrocalcinosis   (menisci/cartilage)   Knee X-ray   Pseudogout (CPPD) 
Joint-space narrowing + osteophytes + sclerosis + cysts   Joint X-ray   Osteoarthritis 
Periarticular erosions, soft-tissue swelling, ulnar deviation   Hand X-ray   Rheumatoid arthritis 
Lung sliding / 'seashore' on M-mode   Lung US   Normal pleura (rules OUT pneumothorax at that spot) 
Loss of lung sliding / 'barcode' on M-mode   Lung US   Pneumothorax 
Lung point   Lung US   Pathognomonic for pneumothorax (transition between sliding and non-sliding)
